purpose: Fentanyl transdermal is a strong prescription pain patch used to treat severe, around-the-clock pain that cannot be managed with other medications. It is typically used for people who need long-term pain control, such as those with cancer or chronic pain conditions. It is not meant for occasional or short-term pain relief.
how_it_works: The patch sticks to your skin and slowly releases fentanyl, a powerful opioid, through your skin and into your bloodstream over 72 hours (about 3 days). Fentanyl travels to your brain and nervous system, where it blocks pain signals so you feel less discomfort. Because it releases medicine slowly and steadily, it helps keep your pain controlled all day and night.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, constipation, drowsiness or sleepiness, dizziness, headache, itching or redness at the patch site, and dry mouth are the most common side effects. Some people may also feel confused or have trouble concentrating.
warnings: This patch contains a very strong opioid that can cause life-threatening breathing problems, especially when first starting or if the dose is too high. Never cut the patch or apply heat to it, as this can release too much medicine at once and be dangerous. Keep patches away from children and pets — even a used patch can be deadly to a child. Do not use alcohol or other sedatives while wearing this patch. Taking too much can cause an overdose, which is a medical emergency. This medicine can also cause dependence and should only be used exactly as prescribed.
typical_dosing: The patch is usually applied to clean, dry, flat skin on your upper arm, chest, or back, and changed every 72 hours (3 days). Your doctor will start you on the lowest dose that controls your pain and adjust as needed. Only use one patch at a time unless your doctor specifically tells you otherwise. Always rotate the spot where you place the patch to protect your skin.
